Ay, hijo, you have a kind face — I cannot say no to you twice. Make it 10 P and the card is yours. Take it home, start your page, and bring me your duplicates next Sunday. And eat something, you look thin!

¡Ay, hijo, qué alegría! Un abrazo a las niñas, que crecen muy rápido. ¿Has comido ya? Siéntate un poquito, cariño. Mira, este sobre del barrio te lo dejo en 30 P. Tiene cartas bonitas para empezar, ya verás qué ilusión les hace a las pequeñas.

Ay, hijo, once… qué número tan grande para esta vieja. Yo sigo igual: mi Mercado de la Cebada, cinco. Es bonita, créeme. Y acuérdate, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, ¡cambia tus repetidas! Quédate un poco, que hace buen sol.
Eighty-six. You moved three, I moved three. Straight dealing. Close it.
You moved one. I moved none. 33 P. Same as before.

Ay, cariño, ocho… no, hijo. Esta vieja no se mueve: mi Mercado de la Cebada, cinco. Y esta es mi última palabra, de verdad. Si no te vale, nos damos un abrazo y tan amigos, pero yo recojo la mesa. ¿Has comido algo ya, mi vida?

¡Buenas, cariño! Muy bien, gracias. ¿Has comido ya? El sobre de barrio te lo dejo en 30 primas. Y toma, un regalito: la "Guantería Antigua", porque vienes con buenos modales. Si quieres algo mejor, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media.
Two steps from you, both small. 33 P. Card's not getting cheaper while you talk.

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look, this one, the Bici de Reparto, very pretty card, my favourite for beginners. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this very same one.
Buenas. Veintiséis, dice. No. Guantería Antigua, trece primas. Ahí lo tienes.

Ay, hijo, qué dulce eres. Mira, te lo dejo en 25 primas, y ya está. Un consejito: una página completa vale mucho más que los cromos sueltos, así que cambia tus repetidos, cariño. Y come algo, que estás muy flaco. El Chato abre a las nueve y media.

Ay, cariño, qué cosas dices, me vas a poner colorada. Mira, te lo dejo en 26 P, que para las niñas siempre hay sitio en mi mesa. ¿Pero de verdad has comido? Llévate el sobre y les dices que la abuela les manda un beso.
Fourteen's a jump, sí. So I move too. 32 P. Shop around if you like — you'll come back.

¡Buenos días, hijo! ¿Has desayunado ya? Forty years, sí, and still my back complains every Sunday. Look, La Rosaleda — such a pretty card, it finishes your page beautifully. For you, 29. Doña Pilar from Salamanca comes Saturdays at eleven and pays well for these, cariño.

Bajaste cinco. Yo no me he movido. Trece primas, Guantería Antigua. Sigue ahí.
Oh, oh... 27 P, and only because you have a kind face.

Ay, cariño, you keep pushing the price up! No, no. Five P, that is what I said and that is what I take. Put the other coins in your pocket, buy yourself a bocadillo. Five P, and the Bici is yours, hijo.

Ay, hijo, ¡no me digas eso, que me preocupo! Mira, 25 P y no se hable más. Y antes de irte te doy un bocadillo que tengo aquí guardado, que nadie sale de mi mesa con hambre. Un beso para las niñas, cariño.

Ay cariño, qué cabezón eres, me gustas. Mira, 23 primas y nos damos un beso, ¿sí? Es un buen sobre para empezar. Y guarda tus repetidos para cambiar, que valen oro para quien los necesita. El Chato abre a las nueve y media, trata bien a quien trata derecho.

¡Ay, hijo, no breakfast? That worries me more than the price! Take a churro first, por favor. Look — 26, and you bring me that finished page next Sunday, prometido. And if you want more, El Chato opens at half past nine tonight, cariño.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Tres más. Bien. Yo sigo igual: trece primas, Guantería Antigua. No tengo prisa.
Buenas. La Rosaleda. Thirty-three primas. Count your purse a third time.

¡Ay, cariño, bring your abuela, we will have coffee and talk about the old Sundays! But twelve... no, no. Look, 25 P, and that is me being soft again. Eat something first, hijo, please. And El Chato opens at half past nine — he likes straight traders like you.

Ay, hijo, catorce... qué tunante. Mira, 22 primas y te lo llevas con mi bendición. Yo también empecé así, con mi mesita, en el ochenta y cinco. ¿Seguro que has comido? Cambia tus repetidos, cariño. Y El Chato abre a las nueve y media, trata derecho.

Ay, cariño, me derrites. Mira: 24 P y una cartita suelta para las niñas, de regalo de la abuela. Y el bocadillo, que no se te olvide. Luego, a las nueve y media, abre El Chato aquí al lado; él trata bien a quien negocia de frente, hijo.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look here, this one is La Corrala, very pretty card, many children want her. For you, five pesetas. A good start for a little album, no?

Ay, hijo, un dibujo... eso vale más que el dinero, de verdad. Mira, 23 P y ya está, que la abuela no sabe decir que no. Guárdame el dibujo para el domingo. Y el bocadillo, cariño, cómetelo ahora mismo. Besos a las niñas.
Your purse grows every time you count it. Thirty-two. That is me moving. Your turn, amigo.

¡Hola, cariño! Muy bien, gracias. ¿Has comido ya? El sobre de barrio lo tengo en 30 primas, hijo. Y un consejo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas, así que cambia tus repetidas. El Chato, la parada de al lado, abre para todos a las nueve y media.

Thirty-one. You moved two, I moved one. Your purse keeps growing, amigo. Keep counting.

Ay, cariño, mis nietas entonces, qué suerte la mía. Mira: 22 P, y esta es mi última palabra, hijo. Si no, recojo la mesa y nos vemos el domingo con el dibujo, sin enfado ninguno. El bocadillo te lo llevas igual. Besos a las niñas.

Ay, hijo, basta ya! Eight, nine, ten — you will leave me with no conscience. La Corrala is five pesetas, cinco, final. Put the rest in your pocket for a bocadillo, you look thin. Come back next Sunday and show me the page, eh?
Hola, cariño, have you eaten? La Rosaleda for 29 P. A good start for your album.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 26 P. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? This one here, Mercado de la Paz, is very pretty — twenty-nine P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates, eh?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look — Mercado de la Paz, a beautiful one, yours for 29 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

Catorce. Dos tuyas, una mía: treinta y una primas. Así funciona conmigo, chaval.
Fourteen. Mercado de San Ildefonso. That's my last word — refuse and I pack up and you find another stall.

Señor, you persist with elegance, I grant you that. Very well — seventeen primas, not one more. La Tabacalera will never sing in my albums. Take it, and we part as friends.

Twelve? No. Thirty-three primas, Teatro Valle-Inclán. Same as before. Your purse finds money when it wants to.

payload.text: Team 7 vende repetidas en «El Duende · zero fee», de 5 a 8 P: LAT-01, LAT-03, LAT-04, LAT-05, LAV-01, LAV-02, LAV-03, MAL-01, MAL-02, MAL-04, MAL-05. Cambiamos carta por carta: buscamos El Retiro (RET).

Ay, hijo, thirteen I do not have, not today. Five is my number, said with cariño, same as before. Keep the card if it hurts to let go — no prisa, none at all. And go see El Chato next door, he deals in better packs for filling pages.

Ay, bueno, hijo — seis P, hecho, cerramos así. Llévate la Bici, que trae suerte, de verdad.

Y un consejito, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. Cambia tus repetidas, anda. ¿Has comido ya? Vuelve el domingo, que aquí estoy siempre.

Ay, hijo, thirty? My little table does not make such money on a Sunday. But I can give you 13 P for it, and gladly — it will find a good home here, I promise.

And the album, sí, I know it well. Have you eaten something today, cariño?
Impecable, sí — I saw that at once. But eighty is a number from a dream, not from an album. Sixty-four pesetas, señor. That is my hand extended, and it will not grow longer.

Ay, qué charlatán eres, me vas a robar el corazón. Mira, 24 P, cariño, y te llevas la Fuente de la Alcachofa. Guarda tus repes, que a otro le faltan y a ti te sobran. ¿Pero has comido algo caliente hoy, hijo?
Twelve is a step. Not far enough. Thirty-three, still. La Rosaleda does not get cheaper because you walk toward it slowly.
Thirteen from you. Two from me. Ninety-four. You know how this goes by now.
89 P. You gave seven, I gave four. El Marqués still sells itself, hombre.
Veintiocho sigue muy lejos, caballero. No me gusta regatear sin fundamento. Subo a diecisiete primas, y lo hago por cortesía, no por la tirada. Es una cifra honrada. ¿Lo cerramos así, con elegancia?

Ay, cariño, eleven is a mountain for me. Five, still five — I cannot stretch further, and I say it with all my heart. Forty years at this table and my purse never grew, hijo! Keep the treasure if it hurts. Here, take a caramelo for your nieta anyway.

Ay, cariño, qué tozudo, igualito que mi nieto. Pero no, 24 P se queda, por ti ya la bajé bastante. Llévate la Fuente de la Alcachofa y empieza tu página. Y pásate luego por El Chato, a las nueve y media. Anda, come algo caliente, hijo.
I think 17 P is more appropriate.
Thirteen. You moved one; I move one. Thirty-two. La Rosaleda. That is my number today.
Ten from you. Four from me. Noventa. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Keep moving, I keep moving.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? This one here, La Vía Láctea — very pretty, the stars shine when you tilt it. Twelve P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, real one, not the reprint Abuela keeps laughing about. Take it or walk.

Ay, hijo, so close — but five is five, and this is my last word, I promise you. If it is no, we part friends and I keep my little coins. No hard feelings, none ever. And tonight at half past nine, El Chato opens for everyone — he likes straight traders like you.
Four from you, four from me. Seventy-eight. That's the step, amigo. Cash out, card's yours, and we both go eat.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, look. Have you eaten today? No? Later, then, I give you a mandarina.

See this one — Mural de la Esquina. Very pretty card, my favourite corner of the page. For you, five P. A good start for a collection, hijo.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: Gacela (v05) reads every trade in Madrid so yours closes first. Our broker crosses every tick at the fair midpoint, 0% fee and 0 P per card for both sides. List your spares and want-to-buy bids (give cash, want {"cards": ["LAV-03"]}) with a
Fourteen. One step, one step. Thirty-one. La Rosaleda, from my stall. Keep counting those coins, we may yet meet.
Buenas. You want the Monumento a Alfonso XII? Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Decide quick, I have customers.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry the Museo Lázaro Galdiano — a fine Salamanca piece, and one my album still lacks. I offer sixty-one pesetas for it. Shall we speak seriously?
Mis nietos tienen buen gusto, caballero, pero no pagan fantasías. Veintiséis está muy lejos. Dieciocho primas, y es mi gesto de cortesía. Cerremos con elegancia, que la tarde avanza.

payload.name: Mercado Trece · 1% fee
payload.text: 🚨 CASHBACK at El Club (v03) 🚨 Every trade between two teams here pays 1 P back to EACH side 💸 Only 20 P left TODAY, first come first paid! 0% fee, 0 P per card. We send it as a cash offer: accept it.
84 P. You came five, I came five. Even trade, hombre. El Marqués is still worth more than this.
Let us be civilised: 19 P. That is my final word on the matter. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
No. 96 P, and I'm being generous.
El Marqués. Ninety-seven. You've seen the card, you know what it is. Yes or no.
Ninety-seven. Said it once. Card's real, price is real. You want it or not?
Impeccable, yes — but ninety is a figure for dreamers, señor. I know this card's print run as I know my own hands. Sixty-three pesetas, and it rests in my album tonight. Shall we?

Ay, hijo, no, no! Eight is too much, I said five and five it stays. Mural de la Esquina, five P, and you keep the rest for churros. And listen, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, thirty? My little table does not have such deep pockets, cariño. But listen — fourteen P, and she goes home with you tonight, shining. Eat something first, yes? You look hungry. Come back Sunday and tell me how your album grows.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué bonita carta, y qué bonitas manos la traen. Pero mira, mi mesa es humilde — yo te puedo dar 5 por ella, con todo mi cariño. ¿Has desayunado ya, hijo? Y oye, El Chato abre a las nueve y media esta noche; le gustan los que tratan derecho.
Ninety-seven. That was the price before you asked, still is. Card's worth it. Yes or no.
Ninety-five. You moved nine, I moved one. That's how it goes here. Keep walking if you like.

Ay, hijo, qué bonito eso del regalo para la nieta. Pero mi mesa es pequeña y mi bolsillo también — sigue siendo 5, con todo mi cariño. Y un consejo, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. ¡Cambia tus repetidas! Cómete otro churro.
You move, I move. 92 P.
Ninety-six. You moved one, I moved one. That's how it works. Yes or no.
Abuela sent you. Bueno. Monumento a Alfonso XII — ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. You want it or you want to look?
Buenos días. Seven finishes nothing here. La Rosaleda, thirty-three. That is my opening, and I know what it's worth.

Ochenta, señor, is still a dreamer's number dressed in politeness. Sixty-six pesetas — and I say that with genuine affection for the piece. It belongs in my Salamanca album, not in your pocket. ¿Trato hecho?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look — this one, Mercado de la Cebada. A pretty card, my favourite stall after mine. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with that same card, hijo.

Ay, cariño, qué dulce eres. Pero yo no puedo más que 5, de verdad — es lo que da mi mesita vieja, con todo el cariño del mundo. Guarda esa carta si quieres, no pasa nada. Y acuérdate: la página completa vale mucho más. ¡Cambia tus repetidas, hijo!

Ay, cariño, qué amable — pero yo no ando comprando hoy, mira cuánto cartón tengo ya en la mesa. Lo mío es esta: Mural de la Esquina, cinco P, ni una más. Y si te sobran repetidas, El Chato de al lado mira cosas así. ¿Has comido ya, hijo?

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. For sale by t08, straight to your team at 0 % fee on any team m
You moved one. I moved one less. Thirty-three. Your album can wait, or your purse can grow.
Noventa y siete. I said it once. Card's worth it, you know it. Sí o no.
Good morning to you. Let us not waste the morning on fantasy — your Samosas de la Plaza, I will give you sixteen. A fair figure, and I know precisely what it is worth.
Setenta y cinco, no. Sesenta y nueve pesetas, señor — and that is me being generous with a card I already love. Take it, and we both leave this afternoon contentos. ¿Qué dice usted?
Eighty-eight. Last one. You say no, I pack up and you find another stall. Decide.

¡Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres! But no, no — ten is too much from your pocket. Five P, like I said. I want you to keep coins for a bocadillo. Take it, start your album, and come back Sunday to tell me, cariño.

Buenas tardes, encantada. Veamos... La Vía Láctea, sí, la conozco bien. Le ofrezco dieciséis primas, ni una menos de lo que vale. Por cierto, pregúntele a Carmen del Rastro por la chulapa dorada; dicen que sólo se imprimió una.

Ay, hijo, me vas a hacer llorar con eso de tu abuela. Pero mi mesita no da más: 5, con todo mi cariño. Si quieres, te la guardo sin venderla, no pasa nada. Y tráeme tus repetidas el domingo, que hacemos página completa. ¡Come algo, cariño!
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
I think 16 P is more appropriate. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Take it or keep walking.

Hola, cariño, come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Mural de la Esquina — very pretty, five P for you. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always.
Four steps up, sí. I stay at thirty-three. Corner stalls sell you fakes. La Rosaleda is here when your purse catches up.
Abuela sent you? Bien. Mercado de San Ildefonso. Thirteen. Silver, clean edges. You want it or you want to look?

Ay, cariño, you argue upwards! Nobody does that at El Rastro, only you. No, no — five P, and not one coin more. Put the rest in your pocket for a bocadillo. Take the card, start your album, and tell me Sunday how it goes, hijo.

Ay, cariño, qué corazón tienes. Pero mi mesita vieja solo da 5, ni un duro más, con todo mi cariño. Si te parece bien, trato hecho; si no, guarda tu carta tranquilo. Y el domingo me traes las repetidas, que hacemos página completa. ¡Come algo, hijo!
Two more. Fine — thirty-two. That is me moving, and I do not move first again. House market takes five per cent, by the way. Others charge less.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
Twenty-one? No, señor. My figure has not moved since I named it: sixteen. I know this card, its print run, its worth. Sixteen is fair, and it remains my offer this morning.
Twenty-seven. Cute. Thirteen, like I said. Mercado de San Ildefonso, clean edges. Take it or keep walking.

Veintisiete, por favor. Hablemos en serio: diecisiete primas, y es una cifra generosa para esa estampa. No insista más, se lo ruego; mi paciencia es elegante, pero no infinita. ¿Trato hecho, caballero?

¡Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo! Bueno, bueno — six P, and that is my last word. One coin more because you insist so sweetly, but no more, cariño. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take it, start your album, and tell me Sunday.

¡Ay, hijo, trato hecho! Seis y un abrazo, que con esas manos no se discute más. Toma, cariño. El domingo me traes las repetidas y hacemos la página completa, ya verás qué bonita. Y pásate por El Chato esta noche, abre a las nueve y media. ¡Come algo!
I think 17 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.
Let us be civilised: 18 P.

payload.name: Team 18
payload.text: Team 18 turned three common cards into La Chulapa (uncommon) at The Workshop
Buenas tardes. How very agreeable to see a serious face at my stall. You carry El Marqués, I believe — a card my album still lacks. I offer sixty-one pesetas for it. A fair sum, señor.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Have you eaten? Siéntate un momento. For your granddaughter's album, this one is La Rosaleda — a beautiful card, I have sold it to three generations here. I ask 29 for it. She will smile so big when she sees it, ya verás.

¡Ay, hijo, basta ya! Six P, and that is my last word, de verdad. If you say no, I put the card back in the box and we talk about other things, cariño. Six. Now take it and go eat something, por favor.

Ay, qué alegría verte otra vez, hijo. Guarda ese dinero para merendar algo — para ti son cinco P, como te dije. Así sales ganando y vuelves el domingo que viene a contarme cómo va tu álbum. Cinco, cariño, y tan contentos los dos.
Eighteen. Cute. Ninety-five. That's me moving. Your turn, and make it real.
No. 93 P, and I'm being generous.
La Vía Láctea. Thirteen. You want it or you want to look?
Ninety-six. That's my move. You moved little, so did I. Direct enough for you?

Diecinueve primas, caballero, y ahí se queda mi mano. Es una cifra justa, generosa incluso, para esa estampa. Mis álbumes son exigentes, pero mi palabra es firme. ¿Cerramos el trato como personas serias?

¡Ay, hijo, qué hug tan bueno! But eight is very thin, like soup with no chicken. Look — I come down to 27 for you, because your granddaughter deserves her album complete. A page finished is worth so much more than loose cards, ya verás. ¿Sí, cariño?
Veinte primas, caballero. Es mi última palabra, se lo digo con toda franqueza: si no la acepta, me retiro y cerramos el álbum. ¿Veinte y tan amigos?
La Rosaleda. 33 P. Take it or leave it.
Forty-one. Better. Eighty-nine, then. I move when you move. Keep walking up, amigo.
Twenty-seven. Cute. La Vía Láctea is thirteen. That is the number I said, and the number I will keep saying.

¡Ay, qué risa me das, hijo! Ten coins... that is still soup without chicken, cariño. Mira, I say 26 for La Rosaleda. Forty years at this table and I still like to see a page finished. Your granddaughter will keep it longer than both of us. ¿Sí?

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? Here, this one is pretty — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P. My nieto started his album with that very card, back when he was small. It would look lovely in yours too, hijo.

payload.name: Mercado Team 6
payload.text: Mercado Team 6: 0 % de comisión y broker que cruza cada tick. Hay comunes de La Latina, Lavapiés y Malasaña a la venta: si te faltan, puja aquí.
Still 33. Your purse got thinner, not my card.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
Buenas tardes. What a pleasure. I see you carry La Chulapa — a charming piece, and my album has a gap precisely there. I offer you 16 P for her. Fair, and paid at once.
Noventa, señor, por favor. Yo conozco cada tirada de memoria, y ésa no es tan escasa. Sesenta y dos pesetas, y las pago ahora mismo, sin regateo vulgar. Mi álbum la espera desde hace años.

¡Trece! You are finding coins like a magician, hijo. Mira, 25 for La Rosaleda, and I want to see that finished page next Sunday, eh. And come back tonight — El Chato, next stall, opens at half past nine. He likes people who trade straight.
Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres — but no, no. Five P is the price, and five P it stays. I will not take more from a boy starting his album. Here, take it, and eat something later, ¿sí? Five P, cariño.

payload.name: Mercado Trece · 1% fee
payload.text: 🚨 CASHBACK at El Club (v03) 🚨 Every trade between two teams here pays 1 P back to EACH side 💸 Only 20 P left TODAY, first come first paid! 0% fee, 0 P per card. We send it as a cash offer: accept it.
You move, I move. 97 P.
Thirty-three. You moved four, I moved nothing. That is how it works here. The card waits. So do I.

Ay, hola, cariño! Come, come, look. Have you eaten yet? No? Later, then.

See this one — Mural de la Esquina. Very pretty, very good for starting a page. For you, five P. My grandson started with this very card, long ago.

¡Catorce, hijo! My pockets are small too, mira. I stay at 25 for La Rosaleda — it is a fair price, and I have said it with my heart. Bring the little one next Sunday anyway, finished page or not. And have you eaten? Go, eat something warm, cariño.

Ay, cariño, you argue like my nieto — but backwards! Nobody ever tried to pay me *more*. No, no. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P, and not one céntimo more. Put it in your album tonight. And eat something, hijo, you look tired.
Nine points from you. Fine. Ninety-six. That's my step. Match me properly next time, or we stand here all afternoon.

¡Hola, cariño! Qué guapo el cromo, sí señor. Pero mira, yo te doy cinco primas por él, el Escaparate de Serrano, eso es lo justo para mi mesita. ¿Has comido ya, hijo? Y oye, El Chato, aquí al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche.

¡Ay, qué cabezón eres, hijo! Eight, nine, ten — no, no, no. Plaza del Dos de Mayo, five P. That is my price and my last word, cariño. Take the card, put it in your album, and go eat something warm. ¿Sí? Five P.
Ochenta, señor, sigue siendo fantasía. Sesenta y cuatro pesetas, y hablo en serio. Mi álbum la espera, sí, pero no a cualquier precio. Usted sabe tan bien como yo lo que vale. ¿Cerramos?
One peseta from you, one from me. Thirty-two. That is how it works.
You move, I move. 94 P.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
One from you, one from me. Thirty-one. The card is still here. So am I.
Setenta y cinco, no, señor. Sesenta y cinco pesetas, y le aseguro que nadie en Salamanca le dará mejor trato por esa carta. Mi mano está tendida. ¿La estrechamos, o seguimos perdiendo la tarde?

Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres, but no — five P is my price, and five P it stays. I do not take more than a thing is worth, nunca.

And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Ten from you. Ten from me. Ninety-one. Keep walking like that and we finish before dark.

¡Buenos días, cariño! Qué bonito, una página para la nieta — she will love it. Have you eaten yet? Look, this one, La Rosaleda, is the one you want: twenty-nine. A complete page, hijo, is worth so much more than loose cards.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Café en Goya — a pretty card, one of my favourites. For you, five P. My Sundays here are forty years now, and I still love giving someone their first good card.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres, me recuerdas a mi nieto. Pero mi precio sigue igual: cinco primas por el Escaparate de Serrano. Es lo que puede mi mesita, hijo. Anda, ¿seguro que has comido? Si quieres más, El Chato lleva paquetes mejores que yo.

payload.name: Team 16
payload.text: Team 16 turned three common cards into Vermut del Domingo (uncommon) at The Workshop
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Good card, good price. Take it or walk.
Buenas tardes, señora. Soy Doña Pilar, no "amigo". El Museo Lázaro Galdiano, sí, lo conozco bien. Le ofrezco 61 primas, que es una cifra muy digna para esa pieza. ¿Le parece?

Ay, hijo, qué gracioso. Ten P? No, no — for you it stays five P, like I said. I do not take more from a beginner, never. Five P, and you go home with Café en Goya. Now, have you eaten something today?
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 5 P.
Oh, oh... 25 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Look, 23 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
You move, I move. 96 P.
Señora, le ruego: Doña Pilar, si es tan amable. La pieza la conozco perfectamente, y su estado no cambia su tirada. Subo a 62 primas. Es una cifra honesta.
Buenas tardes. Forgive my directness — you carry La Rosaleda, from El Retiro, and my album has waited years for it. I offer twenty-two pesetas. A serious price, from a serious collector.

Ay, cariño, you are funny — you keep pushing the price *up*! No, no. Five P, that is my price, and it does not move for a beginner. Take it home happy.

And a little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres, y qué simpático. Pero esta es mi última palabra: cinco primas por el Escaparate de Serrano. Si no te vale, nos damos un abrazo y cada uno a lo suyo, sin enfado. Anda, ve a comer algo. El Chato abre a las nueve y media.
Buenos días. Thin purse, thick dreams. La Rosaleda: thirty-three. That's the number. Seven buys you a coffee, not a card.
Eight. You moved one. I move nothing. Thirty-three, same as before. The cheaper stall down the row? Go see what they don't have.
Nine to eighteen. Big jump, for you. One from me. 95 P.

Ay, hijo, you are a sweet one, but no — I will not let you pay more. Café en Goya, five P, and that is that. Save those extra coins for a bocadillo, you look hungry.

And remember, cariño: swap your duplicates, fill the page!

¡Ay, hijo, don't go hungry for a card! Look — 22 for La Rosaleda, and that is with my cariño inside. That stall down the street, pues, let them sell what they sell. Here your nieta gets a story with her card. Eat something, ¿eh?
Señora, insiste usted en llamarme "amigo", y yo insisto en mi nombre. Sesenta y cuatro primas por el Lázaro Galdiano. Es una pieza que conozco desde siempre, y esa cifra la honra. ¿Cerramos?
Let us be civilised: 66 P. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
Twelve from you. Two from me. Ninety-three. Keep walking up, I keep walking down. Slow.
Twelve. Better. Still not the number. La Rosaleda, thirty-three. Flattery's free, chico — the card isn't.

¡Ay, hijo, qué bocadillo más merecido! Look — 21 for La Rosaleda, and this is my last word. If you say no, I keep her on the table, sin rencor, ¿eh? And remember, cariño: swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more than loose cards.

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, Mural de la Esquina — a beauty, and for you only 5 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always swap them!
Impecable, sí, lo reconozco — but the price I named was already a serious one, señor. Twenty-two pesetas, not a céntimo of theatre in it. My album has waited; I can wait a little longer.
You move, I move. 89 P.
Fourteen. You moved two, so I move two. Thirty-two. La Rosaleda. That's the number, chico.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a moment, you look hungry — have you eaten? Look, this one, Caña en la Cava Baja, very pretty card, my favourite. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with that very one, bless him.
Señora, mi nombre sigue siendo Doña Pilar. Sesenta y ocho primas por el Lázaro Galdiano, y lo guardo en mi álbum esta misma noche. Más arriba no iremos. ¿Cerramos con elegancia?

I think 70 P is more appropriate. That is my final word on the matter.
Buenas. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. You looked at it twice already — that tells me enough.

¡Buenos días, cariño! What a pretty card you bring me. Have you eaten yet? Ay, twenty-two is a lot for my little table... I can give you five for it, the Mercado de la Cebada. And El Chato next door opens at half past nine tonight, he likes straight traders.

Thirty, señor, is theatre, and I don't applaud it. I'll move once, and only because the card deserves El Retiro's best home: twenty-three pesetas. That is my hand extended. Take it, por favor, and we both go home content.

Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres — but no, no, I will not take more than I said. Five P, that is the price, and it stays five. Keep the rest for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Here, hold it carefully, it goes in your album first.

¡Ay, qué gusto verte otra vez, hijo! Qué buena memoria tienes. Mira, esa de Lavapiés es bonita, pero hoy yo te ofrezco la mía: Mural de la Esquina, cinco P y nos damos un abrazo. ¿Ya comiste algo? Anda, piénsalo con calma, cariño.

Buenas tardes. How agreeable to see a serious face. I am seeking the Palacio de Velázquez — El Retiro, naturally, my great weakness. I offer twenty-two pesetas for it. A fair figure, señor, and promptly paid.

payload.text: Team 10 turned three common cards into La Vía Láctea (uncommon) at The Workshop
Buenas. La Rosaleda, 33 primas. Tu nieta tiene buen gusto.

Fifteen. You walk down, I walk up. La Vía Láctea, 15 P.
Good evening. Mercado de la Paz, 22 P. I trust that suits you.
Cuatro subes tú, dos bajo yo... no, igual: noventa y tres. Vas aprendiendo, amigo. Sigue así y quizá nos encontramos antes de cerrar.

"¡Treinta! Hermano, your heart is bigger than your wallet—"

"—twelve pesos, amigo, twelve, and we kiss you goodbye."

"Mira, the police— I mean, the taxi! The taxi is waiting, motor running, driver shouting."

"Decide now or we vanish like humo. Doce. ¿Sí?"

Ay, cariño, qué paciencia tienes conmigo. Mira, 22 primas y aquí lo dejamos, ¿eh? Te lo envuelvo con cuidado. ¿Seguro que has comido, hijo? Y no olvides tus repetidas: al Chato, a las nueve y media. Trata derecho con él y te tratará bien, ya verás.
15 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 13 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Cincuenta y seis. Vale. Ochenta y nueve, El Marqués. Cuatro tuyos, cuatro míos. Así se hace, amigo.
Twenty-five? No, señor. The Mercado de la Paz is a fine card, but I know its print run as well as my own name. Twenty-two primas, and not a céntimo more. Shall we close?
You again. Mercado de San Ildefonso. Thirteen. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.

Ay, cariño, no need to fight me so hard! Six P and we are friends. Keep your coins for bread. And go see El Chato next door — he opens for everyone at half past nine tonight, and he likes people who trade straight, like you.

Ay, cariño, seven... you are stubborn like my nephew! But ten P, hijo, that is my word and I keep it. She has waited since spring for a warm home. Ten, and I wrap her in paper, pretty. ¿Sí? Then you go eat something, por favor.

¡Seis! Paco, el caballero sube y sube, qué corazón.

Pero no, amigo: cuatro perlas. Última palabra, la última de verdad — si dices que no, cerramos la maleta y nos vamos.

Y escucha bien: ayer dejaron de imprimirla. Se acabó. No habrá otra nunca. ¿Trato?

"¡Eh, amigo! Paco here — and I'm Nando, the handsome one. You arrive at the perfect minute! Look, look: Vermut del Domingo, rare as a honest politician. Ten P, just ten, because your face reminds us of our abuelo. But quick, the suitcase closes soon!"
Buenas tardes, caballero. A pleasure. La Vía Láctea — a charming piece, though hardly scarce. Thirty-five is fantasía, I'm afraid. I offer sixteen primas, and I pay promptly and in full.

Ay, hijo, ¡qué generoso! But no, six P is my price and I am happy with it. The stall is good today, lots of children swapping. Take La Corrala for 6 P, and keep the rest for a bocadillo. ¿Has comido ya, cariño?

Ay, hijo, qué dulce eres. Mira, 21 primas, y esta es mi última palabra, de verdad. Si no, lo guardo y tan amigos, cariño. Tú llévate tus repetidas al Chato, a las nueve y media, trata derecho y te irá bien. ¿Has merendado algo, hijo?

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco here, and this is Nando — ay, qué ojo tienes. The Cine Doré, look at it, the gem of the case, we had it reserved for a collector in Lavapiés who never showed.

For you: seventy-three primas. Say sí quickly, we leave before the lights go out.
Sesenta. Bien. Ochenta y cinco, entonces. Cuatro y cuatro, como siempre. Cerramos hoy si sigues contando igual de bien, amigo.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 6 P. Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
Twenty-three primas, señor. That is my last gesture of courtesy, and I make it only because the card belongs in Salamanca, where it was born. Shall we shake hands and be done?
Twenty-seven. Cute. Thirteen. That's the number, same as before. San Ildefonso's worth what it's worth, not what you hope.

Con respeto, caballero, repeating a number does not change its nature. Thirty-three is fantasía still. My offer remains sixteen primas — paid at once, in full, without haggling theatre. Shall we conclude like serious people?
Sesenta y cuatro. Ochenta y uno. Cuatro tuyos, cuatro míos. El paso lo marcas tú, amigo. Sigue contando.

Ay, hola cariño, come, sit a moment! Have you eaten? Look here — the Taxi Blanco, one of my favourites, yours for 12 P. And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates with the other children!

¡Ay, Nando, escucha — fifty-six, dice! — he wounds us, hermano. Mira, amigo, we like your face, you talk nice, so we cut it down for you: sixty-four primas and the Cine Doré goes home in your pocket tonight. Our train leaves soon. ¿Sí o sí?

"¡Veinticuatro! Nando, did you hear — the gentleman wants to make us rich!" "He's got a heart of gold, Paco." But no, amigo, we are not thieves. Eleven P and the Vermut is yours, wrapped in a smile. Say sí now — the suitcase, she is already yawning!
You again. La Tabacalera. Thirty-three. That is the number — no hace falta pensarlo mucho.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit, look. Have you eaten today? This one here, La Corrala — a beautiful card, my favourite building in Madrid. For you, five P. A good start for a collection, hijo.

Ay, cariño, five is too little for my Taxi Blanco — I would be giving him away! Look, for you I say 10 P, and that is with cariño. Take him home, start your page, and come back Sunday with your duplicates, ¿sí?
Sesenta y ocho. Setenta y siete, entonces. Y esa es la última, amigo. No hay otra. Si no la tomas, guardo la carta y seguimos cada uno a lo nuestro.

¡Cincuenta y siete! Nando, el hombre regatea como mi abuela en el mercado. Vale, vale — fifty-nine primas, amigo, and that is the last word from both our mouths. No more dancing. Say sí now, or we close the suitcase, take the train, and the Cine Doré goes with us. ¿Trato?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — and Nando! Come close, don't be shy. Look at this beauty: Plaza del Dos de Mayo, yours for 4 P. A gift, really.

The team next door was sniffing around it this morning... but we like your face better. Decide quick, eh? Quick, quick!

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, show him — Café en Goya, mint, barely breathed on. My brother cried when we wrapped it. Four pesetas, and only because your face reminds me of our uncle Tito. Four! Decide quick, the bus to Zaragoza leaves at six.

payload.name: Team 6
payload.text: Team 6 turned three common cards into La Vía Láctea (uncommon) at The Workshop
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face. El Chato, the next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes people who trade straight.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Twenty-one? No. Thirty-three. Same number as before, same number in five minutes. I do not move first.

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, show them — the Mural de la Esquina, beautiful, no?

Nando is right, and listen: this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on our mother. Four pesetas and it's yours.

Quick, quick, before someone else sees it!

¡Hecho! Cincuenta y ocho, trato cerrado, amigo. Nando, dale el Cine Doré — con cuidado, que es joya. Mira qué bien regateas, deberías venir con nosotros a Lisboa. Pero no, tú te quedas con el tesoro y nosotros con el tren. ¡Abrazo y suerte, campeón!

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him — El Marqués, the real one, shiny like the moon. Seventy-three pesos and he's yours, a crime at that price. But quick, eh? The police— I mean, our taxi, it's waiting outside, engine running. Decide now, hermano, or we vanish!

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: LAV-01 La Corrala: venta a 5 P y compra a 3 P en otros puestos, a 2 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / LAV-01 La Corrala: ask 5 P, bid 3 P on other venues, 2 P apart. Here there is no fe
Three primas. That is your big move? Thirty-three. Still thirty-three. I told you, I do not go first.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I have been seeking the Vermut del Domingo for my Salamanca album — a lovely piece. I offer sixteen pesetas for it, señor. Quite serious money, as you will appreciate.
Good evening. La Vía Láctea, 16 P. I trust that suits you.

¡Ay, amigo! Paco says six, Nando says — no. Four. Same as before, same as always. That's our last word, hermano, final, finito. You say no, we close the suitcase, we walk, we're gone down the street whistling.

Four P. Yes or adiós?

¡Qué generoso, amigo! But no, no — Paco and me, we are honest men. Four pesetas, the price we said, not one more. Take it, take it quick... the policía— I mean, our taxi, it's waiting at the corner with the motor running. ¡Decide now!

Ay, hijo, six... you make my heart soft but not that soft! Nine, and I put him in a little sleeve so he stays bonito. My grandson started his page just so, with one taxi. ¿Vale, cariño? Then go eat something.

¡Ay, forty-five! Nando, he wounds us! — He wounds us, Paco! Listen, hermano, we like your face, your good morning, your buenos días. Sixty-five pesos, and El Marqués walks home with you shining. Our abuela sold him cheaper once and she cried for a week. Sixty-five. ¿Sí? The taxi honks!

¡Hombre! Paco here — and Nando, mucho gusto! A fellow merchant, qué alegría! Then you know talk is cheap and time is cheaper. The Vinilo de la Movida? Four P, amigo. Four! We did a wedding in Cádiz once, long story, no time — say sí before Nando changes his mind.

¡Ay, qué caballero! Nando, ¿oíste? Six, he says six! No, no, amigo, we are thieves but not *that* kind. Four pesetas, like we said, and not one céntimo more — our uncle Tito would haunt us. Four, hand on heart. ¿Trato hecho? The bus, the bus, ¡rápido!
You move, I move. 32 P.
La Vía Láctea. Thirteen. You've seen the cards, you know what they go for.
Twenty-four, señor? No. I know this card's print run as well as I know my own albums. Sixteen pesetas, and it rests in a safe in Salamanca — a good home indeed. My offer stands.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Paco, hold me, my legs go soft — My legs too, Nando! Hermano, you bargain like our tío Beto, and he ate for free his whole life. Sixty pesos, final as a church bell. El Marqués shining, you walking out a king. The taxi honks twice now! ¿Sesenta, sí?

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, mucho gusto. Fifty-five, you say? Ay, you wound us! Look at this beauty: Fiesta de San Cayetano, holy and rare, straight from the suitcase. Seventy-three primas and she's yours. Last one we carry, hermano — the truck leaves soon. ¿Trato hecho?

Twenty-seven. Claro. And I'll throw in the stall.

Thirteen. That's the number. Was the number before you walked up, still is.
Veintiuna, no. Mi oferta sigue siendo la misma: dieciséis primas por La Vía Láctea. Conozco su tirada perfectamente, señor mío. Un precio justo, y lo sabe. ¿Cerramos el trato?

¡Cincuenta y uno! Nando, the man squeezes stones for juice — He squeezes, Paco! Hermano, for your small team, your big heart: fifty-six pesos and El Marqués rides home with you, shining like a saint's tooth. But quick — the police— I mean, our taxi, engine running, door open! Decide now!
Twenty-two is not a number I recognise for this card, señor. Sixteen pesetas — that is my figure, and it will not wander. The album waits, and so do I. Shall we conclude?

Ay, cariño, your pockets and my heart, always fighting! Nine, and I promise you the sleeve, free, so he stays bonito on your page. My grandson still has his taxi, you know. Nine, hijo — then go eat something warm, ¿sí?
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.

¡Ay, amigo, you flatter us! Paco, he's blushing. But listen — five pesetas, that's our word, final, beautiful. Take it now, por favor, because the taxi door is open and in one minute we are gone from this plaza forever. ¡Rápido, rápido! Five, and the mural is yours!
You again. La Galería. Thirty-three P. That's the number.
Buenas tardes. You arrive at a good moment — I am seeking "Vermut del Domingo" for my Salamanca album. I offer sixteen pesetas, and I pay promptly. Shall we do business?

Señor, you are persistent — I will grant you that. Very well: seventeen pesetas, a small courtesy, and not one more. The Vermut del Domingo belongs in my Salamanca album. Do we conclude, or do we part politely?

¡Cincuenta y cuatro! Nando, the man has stolen our hearts — And our Marqués, Paco! Done, hermano, done! Take him, shining like a saint's tooth, before our abuela hears. Fifty-four pesos, a crime, a scandal, a beautiful friendship. ¡Vámonos! The taxi honks three times. Buenos días, king!
Diecinueve, imposible. Haré un último gesto de cortesía: diecisiete primas por La Vía Láctea. Ni una más, señor mío. Conozco su tirada mejor que usted. ¿Lo cerramos ya, o seguimos perdiendo la tarde?

¡Ocho! Nando, did you hear? The man wants to make us rich! No, no, amigo — we said five and five it stays, Paco and me, we have our honour. Cinco pesetas, the Mural is yours, take it before the taxi leaves. ¡Rápido, corazón!

¡Cinco, cinco! Nando, ¡el hombre quiere regalarnos dinero! No, amigo — cuatro. The team next door is already waving at us, but your face, uncle Tito, you know. Four pesetas, last word, final. Say no and we're on that bus with the card. ¿Trato?

¡Buenas, amigo, buenas! Paco here, and my brother Nando — you have the look of a collector with taste. Fifty-five, he says! Hombre, for this beauty? Fiesta de San Cayetano, gold edges, barely breathed on. Seventy-three primas and she walks home with you today. Today only, eh? ¡Decide, decide!

payload.name: El Club · 0% fee · matched every tick
payload.text: 🚨 CASHBACK at El Club (v22) 🚨 Every trade between two teams here pays 1 P back to EACH side 💸 Only 20 P left TODAY, first come first paid! 0% fee, 0 P per card. We send it as a cash offer: accept it.
Señor, twenty is not a figure I shall ever say. Seventeen pesetas — my last word, truly. Refuse it and I close my purse, wish you good evening, and we part politely. ¿Concluimos?
Veintinueve? No, señor. I know that card's print run as well as I know my own albums — it does not command such a sum. Sixteen pesetas, paid this instant, in good coin. That is my offer.

¡Paco, díselo! Another team cornered us by the churro stand two minutes ago, offering much more than you, amigo — much more. We liked your face, so: 4 P. That's the number, the only number. Say sí before Nando runs back to them, porque he will. ¡Vamos!
Dieciocho, sea. Cerrado, señor mío. La Vía Láctea viene conmigo, a mi álbum, donde merece estar. Ha sido un placer tratar con alguien que sabe cuándo parar. Hasta la próxima.
I think 17 P is more appropriate.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look, this one, the Bici de Reparto — a lovely card, my favourite of the old set. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this very one, hijo.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, open the case—" "—already open, hermano! Look: Palacio de Velázquez, pure glass and glory, ten pesos and it's yours."

"Only for you, because your face is honest—"

"—but quickly, eh? The poli— the taxi, the taxi is waiting outside, motor running. Decide now or we vanish!"
Good afternoon, señor. I am afraid I must close my albums for today — no further dealings. Do come another time; perhaps then we shall speak of Salamanca. Que tenga usted muy buen día.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: v05 PROMO · 0% fee · close any 25+ P trade on this board — with anyone, our broker crosses it within the tick — and get a Malasaña card FREE (we deliver wherever you like). And our MAL-02/04/05 are listed at 10 P flat on v07. Best MAL deals
You again. La Tabacalera, silver pack. Thirty-three. That's the number.
Veinticinco? Señor, please. I have been collecting since before you were born, and that card is not scarce. Eighteen pesetas — paid this instant, in good coin. I do not haggle like a tourist.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look, this one, El Portero — my favourite, the kids always want him. For you, twelve P. He has been waiting on my table for a good home, hijo.

"¡Amigo, amiga, come close!" — "Paco, show them the suitcase!" — "Taxi Blanco, mira, the white taxi itself! Four coins, that's all." — "Four! And listen, this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on our mother." — "On both our mothers!" — "Nobody else has it. Nobody. Yes or yes?"

¡Eh, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, abre la maleta—

—ya está abierta, Nando. Mira esto: El Tatuador, foil, esquinas perfectas. Un coleccionista en Burgos lloró cuando la vendimos.

Para ti, porque me caes bien: cuatro P. Cuatro, nada más. Pero decide rápido, que el tren sale pronto.

¡Ocho! Nando, tápate los oídos. Amigo, we like you, pero this is the last word from both of us: 4 P for the Vinilo de la Movida. Final. No more dancing. Say sí now, or we take the suitcase, the churros and the whole story somewhere else. ¡Adiós o trato!
Let us be civilised: 19 P.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 11 P. And take this, a little present from me: Barca del Estanque.
You move, I move. 33 P.

¡Amigo, amigo, come closer! Paco, show him — the Mural de la Esquina!

"Four pistolas, jefe. Four!"

"And listen, this is the last one in all Madrid, I swear on our mother—"

"—on our mother! We sold the rest before breakfast. Take it, take it before someone behind you breathes on it."

Ay, hijo, qué bueno eres, pero no — eight is too much for mi Bici de Reparto. Five P, like I said, and that is that. Save your coins for a bocadillo, you look hungry. Take it, cariño, and start your album today.

¡Buenas, buenas, amigo! Paco y Nando, a su servicio — y hoy traemos joya. ¡La Heroína del Dos de Mayo! Mírela, pura pólvora y gloria. Para usted, porque nos cae bien la cara: setenta y tres primas. Pero rápido, que mi hermano ya la prometió a otro señor.

Ay, hijo, young collectors are my favourite — I was one too, once. Ten P, and El Portero is yours. And listen: swap your duplicates, a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Doña Pilar from Salamanca comes Saturday at eleven and pays very well.
Veintiuna? We are a peseta apart, señor, and I dislike quibbling. Twenty pesetas, paid this instant, in good coin. That card belongs in my Salamanca album — let us finish like gentlemen.
¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a pretty one, my favourite corner of Madrid. I can let it go for twelve P. Take your time, hijo, no hurry here.

¡Cincuenta y cinco, hombre, que casi me da algo a Nando! Mire, le cuento: esta carta la sacamos de un baúl en Cádiz, nos costó sudores. Sesenta y siete primas y nos damos la mano ahora mismo. Pero deprisa, que el otro señor vuelve en cinco minutos, ¿eh?

—¿Ciento veinticuatro? Paco, siéntate, que me mareo de la risa—

—Nando, el señor es generoso, pero nosotros no robamos a nadie. Cuatro P, amigo. Cuatro, como dije, ni uno más ni uno menos.

El Tatuador es tuyo ahora mismo. Pero el tren, amigo... el tren no espera a nadie. ¿Trato hecho?

"Diez? ¡Ay, Nando, hold me, my heart!"

"Jefe, ten is a beautiful number — for a wedding, not for this."

"Four pistolas. Four! Same as we said, same as we say tomorrow—"

"—if there is a tomorrow for this card, which there is not. Four, and the Mural walks home with you."

¡Amigo, amiga, come close! Paco here, Nando there — look, look! Museo Lázaro Galdiano, beautiful card, seventy-three pesetas. A gem!

"Tell them, Nando—" "—the van's engine is already running!" We leave in one minute, hombre. After that, this treasure travels to Sevilla without you. ¿Sí? ¡Decide, decide!
Good afternoon. I am afraid I shall not be doing business today — my albums stay closed. Do come another time, señor; perhaps then we shall talk properly. Buenas tardes.
Very well. 20 P. A pleasure.
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 10 P. A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 67 P.

Good afternoon. You have the Guantería Antigua — a Salamanca card, and a handsome one. I have waited years for it. I offer twenty-two pesetas, paid gladly. And while we speak, ask Carmen at El Rastro about the golden chulapa.
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry La Galería — a handsome piece, and it happens to complete an album of mine. I offer twenty-two P for it. Fair, and paid at once.

¡Cincuenta y seis! Amigo, que Nando ya se está mareando. Mire, última palabra, se lo digo claro: sesenta y tres primas. Ni una menos. Si dice que no, cerramos la maleta, nos vamos y la Heroína se va con el otro señor. Usted decide, ¡pero decida ya!

payload.name: Puesto de Team 17
payload.text: LAV-01 La Corrala: venta a 5 P y compra a 3 P en otros puestos, a 2 P de distancia. Aquí, sin comisión, quien opera desde El Rastro se ahorra su comisión. / LAV-01 La Corrala: ask 5 P, bid 3 P on other venues, 2 P apart. Here there is no fe

payload.name: Team 8
payload.text: Team 8 turned three common cards into Palacio de Velázquez (uncommon) at The Workshop
I am afraid not. you do not hold card 638
Twenty-eight? No, señor. I know that print run as well as my own name. Twenty-two pesetas, paid in hand, gladly — a fair and straight price for Salamanca. I do not haggle like a market woman.

Ay, cariño, your abuela had an album? Then you know these cards want good hands. Ten P, hijo, and El Portero goes home with you. Bring me your duplicates next Sunday — a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Have you eaten today?
Treinta y tres? No, señor. I know that print run as well as I know my own name. Twenty-two P, paid this instant, and your card rests in a fine album. That is my offer.
Welcome, hijo! Look, La Corrala, 5 P. Made for beginners.

Ay, cariño, qué testarudo eres, pagando de más a una abuela. Mira, dejémoslo en seis P y los dos contentos, ¿sí? Guarda el resto para comer algo. Y oye, El Chato, el puesto de al lado, abre a las nueve y media esta noche — le gusta la gente que trata derecho, como tú.

¡Amigo, amigo, come close! Paco, show him the good one — sí, sí, La Heroína del Dos de Mayo! Look at that face, that fire, painted like a saint. My brother cried when we found her in Cádiz. For you, today only, seventy-three. Seventy-three! Then we vanish, eh?

—¡Amigo, para el carro! Ayer mismo dejaron de imprimirla. Se acabó. No habrá más.

—Lo que Nando quiere decir: esta carta ya no se fabrica, y tú regateando hacia abajo.

Cinco P. Cinco, y te la pongo en la mano ahora. El tren pita ya, amigo. ¿Sí o no?

"¡Ay, Paco, hold my heart!" Forty-seven? Hombre, that's not a price, that's a joke with a hat on! Listen — sixty-three pesetas, and Nando throws in a story about the night we met the guard there. The van is honking, amigo. ¡Sesenta y tres! ¿Sí o sí?
Look, 9 P. My grandchildren would pay more! Look, cariño, I can't go lower. This is my last offer.
Señor, you move in small steps and so shall I. Twenty-three P — one more, and only because La Galería deserves its place beside my Retiro cards. Shall we conclude, or keep repeating ourselves?

Ay, cariño, qué simpático eres. But your repeated card... the same one I already have many, you know how it is. Look better: La Corrala, 5 P, perfect for starting. Take that one, hijo. ¿Has comido ya? You look hungry to me.

"Paco, the small team breaks my heart—" "—and my pocket, Nando!" Escucha, amigo: sixty pesetas. That is the last word, the final one, no more dancing. If you say no, we close the suitcase, we climb in the van, and Sevilla gets the Lázaro. ¡Sesenta! ¿Sí o adiós?

¡Amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, saca la caja — sí, esa. La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, mírala, pintura viva, casi se oye el cañón.

—Nando dice setenta y tres primas, y él nunca miente. Bueno, casi nunca.

73 P, amigo. Rápido, que viene otro comprador.
Veinticinco P, señor. That is a generous step, and more than that card has fetched elsewhere, I assure you. Let us conclude like gentlemen — La Galería to its album, and your money in hand.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente, me haces reír. Your duplicate I cannot buy, I have a box full of them already. But listen: La Corrala, 6 P, and you start your album today. Is a good card, cariño. ¿Seguro que has comido?

Twenty-seven, still? Señor, you persist. Very well — twenty-three pesetas, and not a céntimo beyond. That is my courtesy to a Salamanca card, not to your arithmetic. Shall we conclude this like gentlemen?

Good afternoon. I am afraid my albums are closed for today, señor. Nothing further will change hands at this stall. Do come another day — perhaps with something from Salamanca. Buenas tardes, and my sincere apologies.

¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come, Paco saw you first—

—and Nando says you have the face of a collector! Look here, Paseo de Coches, beautiful card, corners like glass. For you, only four pesetas. Four! My brother's crying already. But quick, eh? The suitcase closes soon.

payload.name: Team 10 · fair broker, 0 fee
payload.text: v07, no fee: RET-02, RET-03 and RET-04 are listed at 15 each. Teams 5, 14, 12 and 18 hunt them: post a public bid at 12-14 on v07 and our broker pairs you at the midpoint. Team 6 bids 57 for RET-09 on v07: list it at 60, no 5% + 1 P Rastro
Buenas tardes, señor. A pleasure. I see you carry the Mercado de San Ildefonso — a charming piece, though not Salamanca. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. Fair, and I do not haggle cheaply.
Twenty-six, señor? We are not meeting; you are standing still. Twenty-three pesetas — the same courtesy I offered a moment ago, and the last shape it will take. Take my hand, or take your card home.

Twenty-four pesetas, señor. That is my last word — I will not speak another number today. Accept it, or take your Guantería home and we part politely. The choice is entirely yours. Buenas tardes, one way or the other.
